launch-mo-st-louis-forest-park.summary: St. Louis's 1,300-acre civic park, combining the free Saint Louis Zoo, Art Museum, History Museum and Science Center with the Muny, Grand Basin, Jewel Box, trails, lakes, golf, sports, playgrounds and event grounds.
launch-mo-st-louis-forest-park.hours: Park grounds are open daily 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. Museums, zoo, visitor center, Muny, Jewel Box, concessions, rentals and recreation facilities keep separate schedules.
launch-mo-st-louis-forest-park.parking: Free lots and curb spaces are distributed throughout the park, while the Zoo and Art Museum also operate paid parking. Choose the exact destination before driving; major events and pleasant weekends can close roads or fill nearby zones.
launch-mo-st-louis-forest-park.arrival: The Jones Visitor Center is the best first stop for maps and orientation. Forest Park is too large for one useful arrival pin, so route directly to the Zoo, museum, Muny, Jewel Box, playground or recreation facility you plan to use.
launch-mo-st-louis-forest-park.restrooms: Dependable restrooms are inside staffed attractions and the Visitor Center during their own hours; seasonal facilities serve selected recreation zones. Do not assume every trail, lake or field has an open restroom nearby.
launch-mo-st-louis-forest-park.cost: Park grounds, trails, Nature Playscape and general entry to the Zoo, Art Museum, History Museum and Science Center are free. Parking, special exhibits, shows, golf, rentals, food and selected attractions cost separately.
launch-mo-st-louis-forest-park.accessibility: Major institutions and many paved park routes are accessible, but distances are substantial and grades, road crossings, lawns, construction and event closures matter. The Visitor Center can help identify practical routes.
launch-mo-st-louis-forest-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in ordinary outdoor park areas. Pets are restricted from zoo grounds, museums, the Nature Playscape and posted facilities or events; service-animal rules vary by institution.
launch-mo-st-louis-forest-park.family: The free Zoo and museums, Nature Playscape, Turtle Playground, lakes, seasonal trolley and wide lawns make Forest Park a premier family destination, but trying to cover the whole park in one visit is unrealistic.
launch-mo-st-louis-forest-park.transit: MetroLink serves Forest Park-DeBaliviere and nearby stations, MetroBus 90 crosses the park, and a seasonal park trolley links major destinations. Verify current routes and the final walk to your chosen attraction.
launch-mo-st-louis-forest-park.need: The Boathouse restaurant and its lot are closed during 2026 renovation. Boat rentals and a temporary beer-and-wine garden continue nearby; use Visitor Center parking or street parking and check park alerts, trolley service and institution hours before visiting.

launch-mo-st-louis-gateway-arch-national.summary: The Mississippi riverfront national park containing the 630-foot Gateway Arch, free underground museum, ticketed tram and film, restored Old Courthouse, landscaped grounds, riverboats and downtown connections.
launch-mo-st-louis-gateway-arch-national.hours: Arch grounds and Luther Ely Smith Square are open daily 5:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m. The Visitor Center and museum are generally 9:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m., with extended summer Friday-Saturday hours; the Old Courthouse is generally 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. Holiday exceptions apply.
launch-mo-st-louis-gateway-arch-national.parking: The National Park Service operates no on-site parking. Stadium East Garage at 200 South Broadway participates in a preferred parking program; prepay and expect event pricing or limited supply during Cardinals games and downtown events.
launch-mo-st-louis-gateway-arch-national.arrival: Enter the Arch through the west entrance facing Fourth Street and the Old Courthouse. The legs are exits only. Ticket holders should arrive early enough for the walk and airport-style security screening.
launch-mo-st-louis-gateway-arch-national.restrooms: Public restrooms are inside the Arch Visitor Center after entry and at the Old Courthouse during building hours. The outdoor grounds and riverfront do not guarantee a nearby open restroom at all times.
launch-mo-st-louis-gateway-arch-national.cost: Grounds, museum and Old Courthouse are free. Tram rides, documentary film packages, riverboat cruises, parking, food and retail cost separately; advance tram tickets are strongly recommended in busy periods.
launch-mo-st-louis-gateway-arch-national.accessibility: Grounds, museum and Old Courthouse provide accessible routes and services. The tram to the top is not wheelchair accessible and requires managing at least 96 steps in an emergency; there are no restrooms or benches at the observation deck.
launch-mo-st-louis-gateway-arch-national.dogs: Leashed pets are allowed on outdoor grounds under park rules but not inside federal buildings. Trained service animals may enter public facilities subject to NPS requirements.
launch-mo-st-louis-gateway-arch-national.family: The free museum, Junior Ranger activities, outdoor grounds, Old Courthouse and river views work well for families. Tram capsules are enclosed and compact, and security plus timed tickets add arrival time.
launch-mo-st-louis-gateway-arch-national.transit: MetroLink serves the 8th & Pine and Laclede's Landing areas, and downtown buses reach nearby streets. Walking from downtown attractions is often easier than moving a parked car.
launch-mo-st-louis-gateway-arch-national.need: Tram tickets often sell out during busy summer days. All indoor Arch visitors pass airport-style security with weapons, pepper spray and similar items prohibited; severe weather can suspend tram, grounds or riverboat operations.

launch-mo-st-louis-tower-grove-park.summary: A 289-acre National Historic Landmark and neighborhood gathering park with ornate pavilions, mature trees, playgrounds, seasonal splash features, nature play, sports courts, farmers' markets, concerts and carriage roads.
launch-mo-st-louis-tower-grove-park.hours: Open daily 6:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. Splash pad, Nee Kee Nee stream, farmers' market, carriage rides, events, offices and reservable pavilions use separate or seasonal schedules.
launch-mo-st-louis-tower-grove-park.parking: Free parallel parking is generally available along park drives, with posted one-way and no-parking zones. Large markets, festivals and concerts can fill interior spaces and change traffic patterns, so consider perimeter streets or transit.
launch-mo-st-louis-tower-grove-park.arrival: Use the Central Playground and Roman Pavilion area for the Muckerman fountain, or route to the named pavilion, field, market entrance or East Stream destination. The long linear park has several practical arrival zones.
launch-mo-st-louis-tower-grove-park.restrooms: Restrooms are available at selected year-round or seasonal facilities and near major gathering areas, but not every pavilion or playground has an open building beside it.
launch-mo-st-louis-tower-grove-park.cost: General park access, playgrounds, splash features when operating, courts and ordinary picnics are free. Reservations, carriage rides, vendors, food, programs and ticketed events cost separately.
launch-mo-st-louis-tower-grove-park.accessibility: Paved roads and paths reach major gathering areas, while historic grades, lawns, curbs, crowded markets and nature-play surfaces vary. Check the exact pavilion or feature route before an accessibility-dependent visit.
launch-mo-st-louis-tower-grove-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in ordinary park areas and at Nee Kee Nee under posted rules. Keep pets out of playground equipment, the children's fountain and posted event or food zones.
launch-mo-st-louis-tower-grove-park.family: Central Playground, the Muckerman splash pad, three playgrounds, Nee Kee Nee nature play, basketball and open lawns make this one of the city's strongest free family parks.
launch-mo-st-louis-tower-grove-park.transit: MetroBus routes serve Grand, Arsenal, Kingshighway and nearby neighborhood streets. Select the stop closest to your named feature because walking end-to-end can be lengthy.
launch-mo-st-louis-tower-grove-park.need: Muckerman Children's Fountain typically runs 10:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. from mid-June into fall, weather permitting. Nee Kee Nee runs 10:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m. in timed water cycles. Verify same-day operation and event closures before promising water play.

launch-mo-st-louis-citygarden-sculpture-.summary: A free two-block downtown sculpture garden with contemporary art, lawns, trees, seating, two contemplative water features and a seasonal children's spray plaza.
launch-mo-st-louis-citygarden-sculpture-.hours: Open daily sunrise-10:00 p.m., year-round. The Children's Spray Plaza operates seasonally, generally Memorial Day weekend-Labor Day from 10:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m., subject to weather and maintenance.
launch-mo-st-louis-citygarden-sculpture-.parking: Use metered curb parking or downtown garages. Nearby meters are generally enforced Monday-Saturday 8:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. with two-hour limits; event restrictions and garage rates vary.
launch-mo-st-louis-citygarden-sculpture-.arrival: Citygarden occupies Market Street between Eighth and Tenth streets. Enter from either block and use the sculpture map for named works; the spray plaza is the family destination rather than the reflecting pools.
launch-mo-st-louis-citygarden-sculpture-.restrooms: Citygarden does not provide a dependable full-service restroom building. Plan around open downtown businesses, libraries, museums or other public facilities before settling in with children.
launch-mo-st-louis-citygarden-sculpture-.cost: Garden admission, sculpture viewing, lawns and the seasonal spray plaza are free. Parking, nearby food, tours and downtown events cost separately.
launch-mo-st-louis-citygarden-sculpture-.accessibility: Broad paved routes cross both blocks and most works can be viewed from accessible paths. Wet spray-plaza surfaces, curb approaches, lawn grades, crowds and winter conditions can affect movement.
launch-mo-st-louis-citygarden-sculpture-.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary outdoor paths under posted city rules. Keep pets out of the children's spray plaza, reflecting pools, plant beds, sculpture and food areas.
launch-mo-st-louis-citygarden-sculpture-.family: The spray plaza, colorful large-scale works, open lawns and compact two-block layout make an easy family stop. Caregivers remain responsible around water and sculpture; only the spray plaza is designed for public water play.
launch-mo-st-louis-citygarden-sculpture-.transit: MetroLink's 8th & Pine and Civic Center connections plus downtown buses place Citygarden within an easy walk. It also links naturally with the Arch, Old Courthouse and downtown library.
launch-mo-st-louis-citygarden-sculpture-.need: Split Basin and Voyager Pool are visual water features, not swimming or wading areas. Use only the marked Children's Spray Plaza for water play and verify seasonal operation before changing children into swim clothes.

launch-mo-st-louis-missouri-botanical-ga.summary: A 79-acre historic botanical garden with the Climatron conservatory, Japanese and Chinese gardens, Victorian district, family exploration center, seasonal children's garden, research collections and changing displays.
launch-mo-st-louis-missouri-botanical-ga.hours: Generally open daily 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. with last entry at 4:30 p.m. Early walking, resident-free periods, Children's Garden, conservatories, historic buildings, tram tours and special events use separate schedules.
launch-mo-st-louis-missouri-botanical-ga.parking: Main entrance parking is free. When the main lot fills, use signed free overflow lots near Shaw Boulevard and South Vandeventer Avenue; major evening events may use remote lots and shuttles.
launch-mo-st-louis-missouri-botanical-ga.arrival: Use the main entrance at 4344 Shaw Boulevard for tickets, visitor help and the most direct route to the Climatron. Advance e-tickets are recommended, although walk-up cashless purchase is generally available.
launch-mo-st-louis-missouri-botanical-ga.restrooms: Accessible and family restrooms are distributed through major visitor buildings, including the Sachs Museum, Spink Pavilion and Brookings Exploration Center areas.
launch-mo-st-louis-missouri-botanical-ga.cost: General admission is paid for adults, while children 12 and under are free. St. Louis city and county residents receive designated free periods with proof and capacity limits; Children's Garden, tram and special events may charge separately.
launch-mo-st-louis-missouri-botanical-ga.accessibility: Major visitor buildings and many garden paths are accessible, with wheelchairs and a wheelchair-accessible tram available under current rules. Historic Tower Grove House is not wheelchair or stroller accessible.
launch-mo-st-louis-missouri-botanical-ga.dogs: Pets are not admitted. Trained service animals are allowed under garden rules, although access may be restricted where animal or collection safety requires it.
launch-mo-st-louis-missouri-botanical-ga.family: The Climatron, Brookings Exploration Center, koi, maze and seasonal Doris I. Schnuck Children's Garden offer strong family choices. The Children's Garden is generally open April-October and its splash pad is seasonal.
launch-mo-st-louis-missouri-botanical-ga.transit: MetroBus serves the Shaw and Tower Grove area; rideshare and cycling are practical. Verify the final route because the nearest MetroLink station still requires a transfer or substantial walk.
launch-mo-st-louis-missouri-botanical-ga.need: The Garden is cashless and special events can replace ordinary hours or admission. Resident-free tickets are walk-up and subject to availability; verify the Children's Garden season, splash pad and historic-building hours before a feature-specific trip.

launch-mo-sunset-hills-laumeier-sculptur.summary: A free 105-acre outdoor museum in Sunset Hills combining more than 60 large-scale artworks with lawns, woodland trails, changing indoor exhibitions, family programs and accessible interpretive models.
launch-mo-sunset-hills-laumeier-sculptur.hours: Open daily 7:00 a.m. until 30 minutes after sunset, year-round, except selected major events. Aronson Fine Arts Center and galleries keep shorter Thursday-Sunday seasonal hours and may close for private events.
launch-mo-sunset-hills-laumeier-sculptur.parking: Free parking is available at the lower Rott Road entrance and west entrance. Art Fair and major-event parking uses special off-site or controlled arrangements, so follow event instructions rather than ordinary arrival directions.
launch-mo-sunset-hills-laumeier-sculptur.arrival: Use the lower entrance for Aronson Fine Arts Center, visitor help and the Art Hike Trail, or the west entrance for upper artworks. Download the map because the collection is spread across lawns and woodland.
launch-mo-sunset-hills-laumeier-sculptur.restrooms: Accessible restrooms are available at Way Field, the Carriage House and Aronson Fine Arts Center during their respective access hours.
launch-mo-sunset-hills-laumeier-sculptur.cost: Park grounds, permanent collection and ordinary gallery access are free. Classes, special programs, food and major events such as the Art Fair may charge or require registration.
launch-mo-sunset-hills-laumeier-sculptur.accessibility: Aronson and the education lab are step-free. The paved Central Pathway follows steep natural grades that exceed ADA standards; wheelchairs are available under current checkout procedures and tactile bronze artwork models support visitors with low vision.
launch-mo-sunset-hills-laumeier-sculptur.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in outdoor galleries but may be prohibited during the Art Fair, Laumeier After Dark and other events. Service animals may enter public areas.
launch-mo-sunset-hills-laumeier-sculptur.family: Large-scale sculpture, open lawns, short trails, family programs and the Children's Sculpture Garden support exploration, but most artworks must not be touched or climbed unless an object label explicitly allows it.
launch-mo-sunset-hills-laumeier-sculptur.transit: Direct transit is limited for this suburban site. Verify the full route and return service before relying on bus or rideshare, especially near sunset closing.
launch-mo-sunset-hills-laumeier-sculptur.need: The entire park closes to ordinary visitors during the Thursday-Sunday Art Fair weekend and selected After Dark programming. Check event and gallery notices, and never climb an artwork unless its label specifically permits interaction.

launch-mo-valley-park-lone-elk-park.address: 1 Lone Elk Park Road, Valley Park, MO 63088
launch-mo-valley-park-lone-elk-park.summary: A 546-acre St. Louis County wildlife park where visitors may see elk, bison, deer, turkey and waterfowl from a slow one-way driving route, reservoir overlooks and the wooded White Bison Trail.
launch-mo-valley-park-lone-elk-park.hours: County park gates follow posted daylight hours and wildlife or weather closures. Arrive with enough time to complete the one-way drive before the closing gate; visitor facilities and adjacent attractions keep separate schedules.
launch-mo-valley-park-lone-elk-park.parking: Stay in the vehicle on the one-way wildlife drive except at designated parking, picnic and trail areas. Never stop in a travel lane, approach animals or block gates for a photograph.
launch-mo-valley-park-lone-elk-park.arrival: Enter from Lone Elk Park Road and follow the marked one-way wildlife loop. The elk and bison occupy managed areas; sightings are likely but never guaranteed, and animals may be close to the road.
launch-mo-valley-park-lone-elk-park.restrooms: Restrooms are associated with the visitor and picnic area during posted access. The drive loop and White Bison Trail do not provide facilities at every stop.
launch-mo-valley-park-lone-elk-park.cost: General park entry, wildlife drive, reservoir views, hiking and ordinary picnics are free. Donations, reservable shelters, programs and the adjacent World Bird Sanctuary may differ.
launch-mo-valley-park-lone-elk-park.accessibility: The wildlife drive offers viewing from a vehicle. Picnic and visitor areas provide developed access, while White Bison Trail is a hilly natural-surface route with roots, mud and no step-free equivalent.
launch-mo-valley-park-lone-elk-park.dogs: Pets are prohibited because free-ranging elk and bison create serious safety risks. Do not bring a dog for the drive or trail; qualifying service-animal access should be confirmed directly with county staff.
launch-mo-valley-park-lone-elk-park.family: The wildlife drive can be memorable with children because much of the visit remains in the car. Keep windows and doors controlled near animals, bring binoculars and pair the drive with a short reservoir or picnic stop.
launch-mo-valley-park-lone-elk-park.transit: A private vehicle is the practical way to experience the wildlife loop. Direct public transit and safe pedestrian access are limited, and rideshare is unsuitable for a one-way animal drive without a retained vehicle.
launch-mo-valley-park-lone-elk-park.need: Elk and bison are wild, powerful animals. Remain in the vehicle in animal ranges, never feed or approach wildlife, expect temporary closures, and understand that the park cannot guarantee a sighting on every visit.

launch-mo-maryland-heights-creve-coeur-l.summary: St. Louis County's large lake park with a 320-acre lake, paved loop and connector trails, paddling, sailing, fishing, sand beach area, playgrounds, seasonal splash play, disc golf, fields and reservable shelters.
launch-mo-maryland-heights-creve-coeur-l.hours: Open daily from 30 minutes before official sunrise until 30 minutes after official sunset; vehicle gates generally open at 7:00 a.m. Rentals, water access, splash play, restrooms, concessions and events use separate schedules.
launch-mo-maryland-heights-creve-coeur-l.parking: Use Sailboat Cove on Marine Avenue for lake access or the exact upper-park lot for trails, fields, disc golf, playgrounds and shelters. Busy weekends and races can fill shoreline lots.
launch-mo-maryland-heights-creve-coeur-l.arrival: The lower lake and upper recreation areas are distinct. Route to Sailboat Cove for paddling and the lake loop, or select the named shelter, playground, trailhead or athletic destination before driving.
launch-mo-maryland-heights-creve-coeur-l.restrooms: Modern restrooms are available at selected lake, shelter and recreation areas during posted or seasonal hours, but long trail segments do not have frequent facilities.
launch-mo-maryland-heights-creve-coeur-l.cost: General park, trails, playgrounds, beach area, splash play when operating, fishing access and disc golf are free. Rentals, permits, shelters, concessions and organized activities cost separately.
launch-mo-maryland-heights-creve-coeur-l.accessibility: The paved Lakeview Loop and developed shoreline areas provide accessible choices, while natural trails, beach sand, launch edges, steep upper-park connections and flood debris vary.
launch-mo-maryland-heights-creve-coeur-l.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in ordinary park areas. Keep pets out of splash play, swimming-restricted areas, buildings, crowded events and posted habitat zones.
launch-mo-maryland-heights-creve-coeur-l.family: Playgrounds, seasonal splash play, the flat lake loop, picnic shelters and boats make this a strong family destination. The sand beach is not a supervised swimming beach; obey posted water-contact rules.
launch-mo-maryland-heights-creve-coeur-l.transit: Driving, cycling and regional greenway connections are the practical approaches. Direct transit may not place visitors near the desired lake or upper-park destination, so verify the final route.
launch-mo-maryland-heights-creve-coeur-l.need: Creve Coeur Lake is managed for boating and fishing, not ordinary swimming. Flooding, water quality, heat, high water and events can close trails, launches or features independently; check county notices before a water-focused visit.
